_authority: This file is the authority on what screens a one-page module may contain and what each kind must satisfy. Read it; do not restate it in prose. If a rule changes, change it here.

_markup_contract.slide: section.slide — one per screen, in delivery order. Inactive slides are display:none.
_markup_contract.data-title: required. The screen's own title. The run-script generator reads this.
_markup_contract.data-kind: required. One of the ids below. Drives styling and the generated run script's per-screen line.
_markup_contract.data-block: required. The timetable block this screen belongs to, e.g. "Block A2". The stable reference — slide NUMBERS move, blocks do not.
_markup_contract.data-mins: on the FIRST screen of a block only. The block's minutes.
_markup_contract.data-track: required wherever data-mins is. "theory" or "practice" - which allocation bucket this block's minutes are claimed against. This is the Track A audit trail: the sum per bucket must equal what the programme allocated. It is not a styling hint and it is not editable to make a build look better.
_markup_contract.data-active: required wherever data-mins is. Integer minutes of this block in which the trainee does, decides, produces or says something rather than receives. Track B, a design metric; it changes nothing in Track A. 0 is legal and sometimes honest. Checked by hours/scripts/check_balance.py, which rejects a value above data-mins, a practice block under half active, and a theory block claiming 100 %.
_markup_contract.data-activity: on launch screens only. The activity/task code exactly as the task manifest knows it, bare and undecorated, e.g. "T1" or "GAS601". Never put it on a screen that merely talks about the activity.
_markup_contract.data-cue: optional, instructor-only. Never rendered. Revealed on the instructor's own key. Anything borderline under the audience rule goes here.
_markup_contract._why_no_href: A slide is a delivery screen inside the single page. An <a href> inside one navigates away mid-session, which is the model this architecture replaced - the instructor loses the deck, the progress, the cue and the place. THE DECK ANNOUNCES A TASK; IT NEVER LAUNCHES ONE. The golden deck carries 27 slides and zero links, and says it in words: "Now a task. Open the tablets - Module 1, task GAS101." Use .act-now for that line. The route to the task lives on START_HERE and on the landing, both OUTSIDE the deck. ETPB3 shipped 17 launch buttons inside slides and the treatment was on its way into the shell before check_static.py caught it; the driven sweep had already printed linksInsideSlides: 17 and it was read past. A count in a report is a finding.

kinds.purpose: What this module is and what the day looks like. One per module.
kinds.fill_target: sparer than the floor is allowed — an opener that fills 95% is shouting
must_have: the day's shape in one line
must_not_have: a document index
a list of what is coming, screen by screen

kinds.purpose: The subject. Full professional register; the vocabulary is the competence.
must_not_have: instructor cue text
an internal code in the visible slide-kind line

kinds.purpose: Announce a task or drill and tell the room what to open. Carries data-activity.
kinds.fill_target: 85-100%; a launch screen is usually at ceiling
must_have: the activity code as the room will see it
an .act-now line naming what to open and its code - NOT a link
must_not_have: how it is marked in detail — that is the marking screen
the count of screens in this block, which will not fit; the generated run script carries it instead
an <a href> of any kind - see _markup_contract._why_no_href

kinds.purpose: The run of a practical, paged across as many screens as it takes. In the old model this was a separate document; now it is screens.
must_have: the kit as a physical list first
the abort conditions at the foot of the run
an .act-now line naming what to open and its code - NOT a link
must_not_have: setup below the steps — a person who has never run this works left to right
an <a href> of any kind - see _markup_contract._why_no_href

kinds.purpose: A short piece of bench or bench-adjacent work that happens inside the teaching flow rather than in its own practical hour. Observed, not graded. Carries data-activity and data-track="practice".
must_have: the drill code as the room will see it
what the trainees physically do and with what
an .act-now line naming what to open and its code - NOT a link
must_not_have: a grade or a pass mark - that is what practical-run is for
minutes that are really exposition wearing a drill label
an <a href> of any kind - see _markup_contract._why_no_href
kinds._why: Added after ETPB3. Four of its blocks were already bench work delivered under a theory label, which under-claimed the practice allocation and made the active-learning figure look worse than the module actually was. Without this kind the only honest options were to mislabel them or to inflate P1-P7 with 20-minute entries that are nothing like an 80-minute build.

kinds.purpose: What is marked, in the trainee's own hearing. The criteria stay; the craft of marking moves to data-cue.
must_not_have: marking technique
remediation routes
a second-person "you" that means the instructor

kinds.purpose: What the room concluded. A screen, not an unrecorded conversation — otherwise the block has no screen and vanishes from the day.
must_not_have: a script of what to say

kinds.purpose: What was covered. One per module or one per day.
kinds.fill_target: sparer than the floor is allowed

kinds.purpose: The module check. ALWAYS the last screen.
kinds.fill_target: sparer than the floor is allowed
must_have: the pass rule as the trainee needs it
an .act-now line naming what to open and its code - NOT a link
must_not_have: any link
anything recorded on this screen
the word "record"
the word "score"
an ILO code or a provenance note
an <a href> of any kind - see _markup_contract._why_no_href
kinds._why: The check screen is read by the room while they are being assessed. Marking and recording are the instructor's job on the instructor's own device.

runner_steps._note: The step runner on the landing screen survives, but collapses to about two steps. It announces the day; it is not the thing you click through.

shape.title: Open the presentation and finish it
shape.mins: the module's REAL minute total, added up from data-mins

runner_steps._mins_why: Every step carries mins:. One module shipped a step without it and rendered with no duration badge while every other module showed one — the omission is invisible in the source and obvious on screen.
